translit:
|| Ath Shri Vaishnav Jivandasna Doha ||

Mathura mahalo desh | Kathiyavade katamb vase ||
Aayo Gurjar khand | Santo tane melavade ||1||

Jot julaho pragatyo | Kiyo nam prakash ||
Ved mathi makhan liyo | Pandit pive sarva chhas ||2||

Kalima Krishna ke Kabir | Jene vat ughadi vedo tani ||
Chalyo saghalo sath | Chhipo Pipone Rohilo ||3||

Raghvir dije eh | Jene Dasharath tano daladra hanyo ||
Andha tano aparadh | Nivari nishchal karyo ||4||

Hari haththi ma mel | Aa var aapanpu dakhavo ||
Tote vadhe tuj | Aatam algo kaha jase ||5||

Jam sarikho sadh re | Jota koy dise nahi ||
Aatam tano aparadh | To doshan kahasu dakhavo ||6||

Laj kaha gai rand | Motai masana kam hase ||
Tan jali jase chhar re | Tare saga sambandhi kaha jase ||7||

Bag bagicha chit dhare | Chhand diyo anurag ||
Hari charan vimukh padyo | Svang dharyo verag ||8||

Antargat adar nahi | Mukh kahat hai aav ||
Daman bandhi ladiya | Gadheka svabhav ||9||

Adar van agha dhase | Shvan swarupi sadh ||
Mandir teh masan | Mada dhandhole murakha ||10||

Bhat bhane je duhada | Man motai Mira tani ||
Maram nav jane murakha | Masana jam dhani ||11||

Mira motaiya chhand de | Dhar bandagisu chant ||
Van bandagi kyau paiye | Piu purvala mant ||12||

Aatam ola le | Nigal Narayan tana ||
Panagi pap tani | Bhitar bhijes nahi ||13||

Rajput rano rane | Khatravat vana sahu khatari ||
Nahi Jagdishni jot | Jam ujad deval patari ||14||

Harijanku hushe male | Ninda kare gumar ||
Kot kalp narake pade | Vako var na par ||15||

Guru malyo gumar | Karma eke nav kato ||
Vat malyo vatpad | Vahar deyanta mukh dato ||16||

E daive didho dand | Jug sacharachar bholavyo ||
Jap tap tirath dan | Tame sab jug rolavyo ||17||

Kanto hath Kabirke | Sakal dharma taha toliyo ||
Jap tap tirath dan | Ta mule mitho choliyo ||18||

Kabir kede pragate | Jagma Jivandas ||
Dhaja bandhi dharma dridhaviyo | Jam kinkar pame tras ||19||

Trikam tahare nam | Tribhuvan tatkshan tare ||
Akaran karan avinash | Daman bandhyo rade ||20||

Damodar tu dayal | Jene giri Govardhan kar dharyo ||
Baliko sarvas le | Shu vipra Sudama ghar dharyo ||21||

Damodar daman bandhiyo | Makhan karan mat ||
Jamala Arjun karane | Te koe na jane ghat ||22||

Hari bhajane hushiyar | Pachho pag nar ka kare ||
Bhage kaiso adkar | Je pret joni avatare ||23||

Dant kadhe daladriyo | Hari bhaje jase rog ||
Rahya khand khand mahe vyap re | E bhuta tana sanjog ||24||

Parmeshvar tanu praman | Te sant samagame pamiye ||
Maya moh ahankar | Tethi vedana vamiye ||25||

Maru taru aapanu | Ehane eh aparadh ||
Maya thorki thor hai | Phokat khanche bhar ||26||

Hari sambhare hath bharase | Taharo manavi ||
Maya amulyak mal | Jam machh jhile Jahnavi ||27||

Hu tale Hari nam | Aaphanie tare aavashe ||
Kot janmana karma | Te sant sangat mukavashe ||28||

Indri tana aparadh | Pranme pachha phare ||
Grath na lage kai | To murakh man sanso kare ||29||

Matipanu man mahe | Rahese taru bapada ||
Jab jam grese kesh | Tare bhajase saghala aaphara ||30||

Aapo aatama aap | Jam sadguru charane ugare ||
Tare nathi kaso bhar | Jam marjivo dariye pade ||31||

Manani moti uk | Janu mune Madhav male ||
To Prahlad keso aparadh | Je sant sangatma nav bhale ||32||

E shu kidhu andh | E samvad te shane karo ||
Chhari Hari motai | Jiv motai ko ugaro ||33||

Hari kirtan hushe kare | Hansi kare gumar ||
Hathi kero navano | Mathe ghale chhar ||34||

Parbrahmsu kare prit | Aatam sudho she na kare ||
Marvu chhe nirvan | To andha algo shu phare ||35||

Khoto e sansar | Manma nayan na aavate ||
Ko mehari ko may | Em sahu ko pachi mare ||36||

An bole to aapharo | Bahu bole bahu karma ||
Hasi bole Hari dassu | To kahiye gurugam ||37||

Jo Hari bhagtansu het | To nagan hoy nachavo ||
To chhute sansar | Nahintar kanye pachi mare ||38||

Kukar kotak var | Aa var manav avataro ||
Ram bhaje to par | Nahintar ehaj avasaro ||39||

Udharo kaiso abujh | Jo guru sabad shravane sunyo ||
Kori dharti bij | Pan meh vuthe mahi ma phalyo ||40||

Ochhi nadi nir | Bhadarve sabe bhari ||
Tyu kal kaleja mahe | Maram na jane manavi ||41||

Vichhan tano vivachar | Mritti mahethi upaje ||
Maram na jane kai | Achet budhe thayo andhalo ||42||

Kukar kapali ka kare | Ram kahene sadh ||
Pet tana parpanch | Sikh sakha upadh ||43||

Bhajananand bhule pade | Sanakadik dei sadh ||
Ajamil kushal padi | Gaj gunaka aur vyadh ||44||

Duniya sab daladri bhai | Hari chali Hari nam ||
Dasi kero betado | Kun palav pakade Sham ||45||

Makhan chhande murakha | Valove sarav chhan ||
Nam Gangodak chhar kare | Mutar kare osan ||46||

Matha upar mand | Jam chhatra chhaya kare ||
Janu motero thay | Kaj amaru to sare ||47||

Kukar katako nankhate | Shu purvaj tara pamashe ||
Harijansu kar het | Je vedana saghali vamashe ||48||

Davo kare so daladri | Rude nahi vishvas ||
Ek nardave Narhar bhaje | So kahie nij das ||49||

Suto saghalo sath | Dharan mahe ghughuve ||
Rakha kare Rughnath | Upar jam kankar phare ||50||

Matha upar mand | Jam kankar chhaya kare ||
Jane motero thay | Kaj amaru to sare ||51||

Malatu malatu aane | An malatu arano kare ||
Avali savali ser | Phogat ka e pachi mare ||52||

Mata to Sita khari | Or mata maho mai ||
Agha le bolayke | Pichhe mele khai ||53||

Mat bhai kamat | Bandhav bel koi nahi ||
Put bhayo kaput | Kul lajayo kamani ||54||

Katamb dise kod | Pan Sham snehi koi nahi ||
Ka e abhadave aap | Bheti murakh manavi ||55||

Andhare ujed | Je sant samagam manavo ||
Ujede andhakar | Je aandevsu manavo ||56||

Murakh nahe Jahnavi | Aabhadchhet algi kare ||
Aabhadchhet aapa mahe | Tuj sarikhado tetale ||57||

Nari sathe neh | Te nar yaha na aavasho ||
Aapo rahese taha | Aabhadchhet na laavasho ||58||

Nari nirbal rup chhe | Pan puri parpanch mahi ||
Sant virodhe kubada | Puri chhandi tahi ||59||

Nari narsu ruthi phire | Bhagtansu virodh ||
Nathi kahi na ugare | Jam pendelo khoj ||60||

Sapan jaise phuphave | Nari murakh mudh ||
Je je vachan nikase | Te padase tahane mund ||61||

Puthe apradhan ka padi | Murakh nar achetan ||
Sant sangat Hari bhajan bin | Bhale jamake khet ||62||

Nari neh na todiye | Bhala bura tohe kanth ||
Pativrata piuku bhaje | Vyabhichari anant ||63||

Nari kidhi tag | Mundiye karyu matipanu ||
Pichhe aave vaj | Je antaskaran mahethi utari ||64||
translation:
Heading: Here begin the dohas (couplets) of Shri Vaishnav Jivandas.

1. The land [of his origin] lies within Mathura; his family dwells in Kathiawad. He came to the Gujarat region, to the gathering-place of the saints.

2. The Light appeared as the weaver [Kabir]; he made the Name shine out. He churned the Vedas and took the butter, while the pandits all drink the buttermilk.

3. In the Kali age Krishna is Kabir, who threw open the road of the Vedas. The whole company walked it after him: Chhipo (the cloth-printer), Pipo and Rohilo.

4. Give this [praise] to Raghuvir, who destroyed Dasharath's destitution. He warded off the offence against the blind ones and made [him] unshaken.

5. Do not let go of Hari's hand; this time show that you are His own. If you fall short, the loss grows against you — where can the soul go, apart [from Him]?

6. Look where you will, no sadhu of that measure is seen anywhere. The offence belongs to the soul itself — so on whom will you lay the blame?

7. Where has your shame gone, wretched one? What use is greatness at the burning-ground? The body will burn to ashes — where then will your kin and relations be?

8. He sets his mind on gardens and groves and has cast off loving devotion. He has fallen away from Hari's feet and put on renunciation as a costume.

9. Within there is no respect, yet the mouth says, "Come in." Roped up and loaded with burdens — that is the donkey's nature.

10. Unhonoured, he pushes himself forward — a sadhu in the shape of a dog. That temple of his is a burning-ground; the fool rummages among corpses.

11. The bard recites his couplets, his mind full of the grandeur of a lord. The fool does not know the secret: he is master only of the burning-ground.

12. O lord, give up your grandeurs; set your thought on worship. Without worship, how is it to be gained — the Beloved, the ancient mantra?

13. Let the soul take shelter — the hold ("nigal") that is Narayan's. Then the scum of sin will not soak you within.

14. A Rajput lord stands in battle; without true kshatriya-hood all his assurance is empty. Where the light of Jagdish (Lord of the world) is absent, it is like a dancing-girl in a deserted temple.

15. [One man] meets Hari's devotees with eagerness; the arrogant one slanders them. He falls into hell for a crore of kalpas — for him there is neither shore nor end.

16. He found a guru who was himself arrogant, and not one karma was cut away. On the road he met a highway robber, and while he cried for help his mouth was stopped.

17. Fate has laid down this penalty: the whole world, moving and unmoving, has been deluded. In japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity the whole age has been tumbled about.

18. The balance is in Kabir's hand, and there all the dharmas were weighed. Japa, austerity, pilgrimage and charity — at their very root salt was rubbed in.

19. After Kabir, Jivandas appeared in the world. He raised the banner and made dharma firm, and Yama's servants are seized with terror.

20. O Trikam (Krishna), by your Name the three worlds cross over in an instant. Doer of the undoable, imperishable One — bound with a rope, you wept.

21. Damodar, you are compassionate, you who held up Mount Govardhan on your hand. You took away the whole of Bali's wealth — and what did the brahmin Sudama keep in his house?

22. His mother bound Damodar with a rope for the sake of butter. It was for the sake of the twin Arjuna trees; no one knew that design.

23. Be alert in the worship of Hari; why does a man draw his foot back? What claim is left in his lot, who is born into the ghost-birth?

24. The wretched one bares his teeth [in mockery]; but worship Hari, and the disease will go. It has spread through region after region — this is the company of ghosts.

25. The proof of the Supreme Lord is obtained in the company of saints. Maya, delusion and egotism — the anguish that comes of them is cast away.

26. "Mine, yours, ours" — this very thing is the offence. Maya stays in its own place; for nothing a man drags the load.

27. Remember Hari and your hands will be filled, O man of His. Maya is merchandise of no worth — [live] as the fish swims in the Ganga.

28. When "I" is removed, Hari's Name will come to you of its own accord. The karmas of a crore of births — the company of saints will make you lay them down.

29. The offences of the senses turn back before a bow of salutation. Not a knot of it clings to you — yet the fool's mind goes on doubting.

30. Your self-importance will stay only inside your own mind, poor wretch. When Yama seizes you by the hair, all your swagger will break.

31. Give your own self away, as one is saved at the Sadguru's feet. Then there is no weight upon you, as the pearl-diver plunges into the sea.

32. The mind's great longing is, "may Madhav meet me." Then what offence was Prahlad's, that one should not mingle in the company of the saints?

33. What have you done, blind one? Why do you carry on this argument? Having thrown away Hari's greatness, who was ever saved by the greatness of the jiva (individual soul)?

34. [One man] sings Hari's kirtan (hymn) with joy; the arrogant one laughs at it. It is like an elephant's bath — afterwards it throws dust on its own head.

35. Make love with Parbrahma (the Supreme); why not make the soul straight? Death at the end is certain — then, blind one, why do you wander apart?

36. This world is false, yet it does not settle in the mind or before the eye. One says "my wife", another "my mother" — and so everyone frets himself to death.

37. If he does not speak, it is stiff pride; if he speaks much, it is much karma. If he speaks smilingly with Hari's servants, then we call it gurugam (the understanding received from the guru).

38. If you have love for Hari's devotees, then dance stripped bare [of pride]. Then the world lets go of you; otherwise why fret yourself to death?

39. A crore of times you were born a dog; this time you are born a man. Worship Ram and you cross over; otherwise this was your one chance.

40. What deliverance is there for the dull one, though he heard the guru's word with his own ears? [It is] seed on dry ground: the rain fell, but nothing bore fruit in the earth.

41. A river low in water is brimful in the month of Bhadarva. So death sits within the heart, and man does not know the secret.

42. Consider the scorpion: it is born out of the earth itself. [Man] knows nothing of the secret; with unheeding wit he has gone blind.

43. Why play the dog and the skull-carrying ascetic? Say "Ram", O sadhu. These are frauds for the belly's sake; such teaching, friend, is only trouble.

44. Even Sanaka and the others, called sadhus, fell away from the bliss of bhajan (devotional song). Yet Ajamil fared well, and so did the elephant, the courtesan and the hunter.

45. The whole world has been made destitute; it has lost and walked away from Hari's Name. [But] the serving-maid's son — who else caught hold of Shyam's hem?

46. The fool leaves the butter and churns the dregs alone. He turns the Name, water of the Ganga, into ashes, and takes urine for his remembrance.

47. Set [Him] above your head, as a parasol casts its shade. I think: let Him be reckoned the greater, and then our work is accomplished.

48. By throwing scraps to a dog, will your forefathers receive anything? Give your love to Hari's people — that will drive away all your anguish.

49. He who makes claims is a pauper; there is no faith in his heart. He who worships Narhar with one sole claim [on Him] — call him His own true servant.

50. The whole company is asleep, snoring in its worldly hold. Raghunath keeps watch, while above, Yama's messengers prowl.

51. Set [Him] above your head, as Yama's servants cast their shadow. He knows he is made the greater, and then our work is accomplished.

52. What comes to hand he gathers in; over what does not come he makes a quarrel. Lanes crooked and straight — why does he fret himself to death for nothing?

53. True motherhood is Sita's; other mothers are mothers only among themselves. They call you forward with sweet words, and then drop you into the pit.

54. The mother has turned unmotherly; no brother is a support. The son has turned unworthy; the woman has shamed the family.

55. The family looks a delight, but there is not one who loves Shyam. Why defile yourself, foolish man, by embracing them?

56. Light within darkness — that is to enjoy the company of saints. Darkness within light — that is to take pleasure with other gods.

57. The fool bathes in the Ganga and holds others off as untouchable. The defilement lies within your own "I" — and you are just that much.

58. The man whose love is bound to woman — let him not come here. Your "self" will stay behind there; do not bring that defilement [here].

59. Woman is weak in form, but she is complete in guile. Those crooked ones who set themselves against the saints — she has forsaken them utterly there.

60. A woman goes about angry with her husband and hostile to the devotees. Though she flees she is not saved at all — she is tracked like a footprint already pressed in.

61. As a she-serpent hisses, so does the foolish, dull woman. Whatever words come out of her will fall back upon her own head.

62. Why have you fallen behind as an offender, foolish and senseless woman? Without the company of saints and the worship of Hari, one is mingled into Yama's field.

63. O woman, do not break the bond of love; good or bad, he is still your husband. The faithful wife worships her lord alone; the unfaithful one has endless [men].

64. The woman has cut the thread; the shorn one took on airs of self-importance. Afterwards the blow comes back on her, who has fallen out of the inner heart.
